version.changelog: 三个skill统一线性工作流结构，版本升至3.1.1

llm.summary: This memory-extraction skill clearly says it saves conversation details, but it can do so automatically and broadly enough that users should review it before installing.

dimensions.detail: Requested access to session history plus FileRead/FileWrite/FileEdit is partly purpose-aligned, but heartbeat and conversation-ending triggers make persistence possible without a fresh explicit user command.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains only a SKILL.md Markdown instruction file and no executable scripts, dependency installation, remote payload retrieval, or install-time commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads recent session messages with no message-count limit, stores user decisions, preferences, project constraints, and external references, and does not require a preview or confirmation before writing extracted items.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill appends long-term memory files and an index under memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md, including possible URLs, accounts, tools, and paths, with no described deletion, rollback, expiry, redaction, or approval workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: extract important conversation memories into topic files and update a MEMORY.md index. The same purpose necessarily involves reading session context and writing persistent memory, which is sensitive but disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the agent automatically saving selected conversation details to persistent memory. Prefer using it manually with a preview/confirmation workflow, and avoid it for chats containing secrets, private account details, sensitive URLs, or instructions that should not influence future sessions.
llm.findings:
[SSD-3] expected: Long-term storage is central to the skill, but the artifact confirms broad retention categories including external-system references and unlimited recent-message review, so the concern is accepted as a Review issue rather than malicious behavior.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The artifact confirms automatic extraction on generic ending phrases and heartbeat checks; this automatic write path is under-scoped for a persistent memory skill because it lacks explicit confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: The artifact discloses that memories are written to files and indexed, but the warning is not prominent and does not explain review, disablement, redaction, or deletion controls.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese triggers and fixed Chinese output are visible and consistent with the skill text; this is a usability/localization note, not a security driver for the verdict.
[T02] unexpected: The static finding is supported in part: conversation-derived text can be appended into persistent memory and indexed without validation or approval, creating a realistic memory-integrity risk. The artifact does not show code execution, exfiltration, or OS-level privilege escalation.
